outlook: Grains pulled back overnight ahead of the Thanksgiving break: as of 6 a.m. CT January soybeans were down 11 cents near $12.23 after Tuesday's climb to a new monthly high, March corn was down 1¼ cents, and March Chicago and Kansas City wheat were each off about 4½–4¾ cents. A firmer US dollar and sharply lower stock-index futures weighed on trade ahead of this morning's October PCE inflation report, and news of new Section 301 tariffs on China added uncertainty. Tuesday's closes were December corn $4.34, December Chicago wheat $5.69¾, Minneapolis December spring wheat $6.36¾ and ICE January canola C$773.20; other prices shown are those Tuesday closes. US markets are closed Thursday and close early Friday, and December contracts are being rolled ahead of first notice day Monday.
